item.title: Birth Order Study Raises Questions Over Missing Low-Income Families
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new study examining links between birth order and disease risk has drawn scrutiny from researchers over who was included in the analysis. The research excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid, potentially skewing results and limiting what the findings can tell us. The study looked at connections between a child's position in the…
item.content:encoded:
A new study examining links between birth order and disease risk has drawn scrutiny from researchers over who was included in the analysis. The research excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid, potentially skewing results and limiting what the findings can tell us.

The study looked at connections between a child's position in the family—whether they're firstborn, middle, or youngest—and their susceptibility to various diseases. While the research produced measurable results, experts point out that leaving out lower-income families fundamentally compromises the validity of those conclusions.

"A more complete picture would require including all income levels in future research," researchers cautioned. Without data from uninsured and Medicaid-eligible populations, the study may only reflect patterns among insured, higher-income families—a significant limitation when trying to draw broad conclusions about disease risk across the general population.

The findings underscore a broader challenge in medical research: ensuring study populations are representative enough to produce reliable, applicable results. Experts say future investigations into birth order and health outcomes should make inclusive recruitment and diverse income representation a priority from the start.

item.title: Commanders Add Stefon Diggs to Bolster Receiving Corps

item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders are making a significant move to strengthen their offense, acquiring wide receiver Stefon Diggs as they prepare for the upcoming season. The addition addresses the team's need for proven receiving talent and gives quarterback options at the receiver position.

The move comes amid separate concerns around Brandon Aiyuk, whose behavior has drawn scrutiny from multiple NFL teams. According to reports, several franchises have privately expressed concerns about Aiyuk's locker room fit and how he might integrate with teammates, raising questions about his future in the league.

With Diggs now in the fold, the Commanders are looking to build a more cohesive and competitive receiving group. Diggs brings established credentials and experience at the position, having been one of the NFL's more consistent wide receivers in recent seasons.

item.title: Senate Confirms Dr. Erica Schwartz as CDC Director
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Wednesday. Schwartz will now lead the nation's top public health agency, which is responsible for disease prevention, outbreak response, and broader public health initiatives. As CDC director, Schwartz will oversee the agency's response to…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Wednesday. Schwartz will now lead the nation's top public health agency, which is responsible for disease prevention, outbreak response, and broader public health initiatives.

As CDC director, Schwartz will oversee the agency's response to infectious disease threats, coordinate with state and local health departments, and manage the CDC's role in national emergency preparedness. The position is critical to how the federal government addresses public health crises, from seasonal flu outbreaks to pandemic response.

The confirmation comes as the CDC continues to play a key role in monitoring disease trends and providing guidance to healthcare providers and the public. Schwartz's appointment follows a comprehensive Senate confirmation process.

item.content:encoded:
Cesar Gastelum, a TikTok influencer with over 600,000 followers, was killed in a shooting outside a restaurant while livestreaming to his audience. The incident occurred as Gastelum was broadcasting with two friends when gunfire erupted.

Authorities responded to the scene and launched an investigation into the fatal shooting. Details about the circumstances leading up to the incident remain under investigation as police work to identify a motive and any suspects involved.

Gastelum had built a significant following on the social media platform, and his death has drawn attention to safety concerns during public livestreaming events. Investigators are gathering information from witnesses and reviewing footage from the incident.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Public Schools kept students away from Ransom Middle School on Tuesday morning after receiving an unspecified threat, according to Cody Strother, the district's communications coordinator.

Law enforcement responded to investigate the threat while students and arriving parents were temporarily rerouted to nearby Kingsfield Elementary School. Strother did not provide details about the nature of the threat or whether it was determined to be credible.

The school district's swift response follows standard safety protocols for handling such incidents. No information was immediately available about when students would be allowed to return to campus or the outcome of the law enforcement investigation.

item.content:encoded:
Federal prosecutors in Northern Florida have secured 53 convictions of undocumented immigrants over the past three months, according to U.S. Attorney John P. Heekin. The convictions, which span from July through late September, represent an intensified enforcement effort in the region covering the Pensacola area and surrounding counties.

The cases fall under federal statutes addressing illegal entry and presence in the United States. Heekin's office did not immediately provide details about the specific charges, sentencing outcomes, or the nationalities of those convicted.

The enforcement action reflects broader federal immigration policy priorities. The Northern District of Florida, which includes Escambia and Santa Rosa counties, has become an active jurisdiction for immigration-related prosecutions in recent months.

item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida is welcoming two National Merit Finalists to campus this fall, continuing a steady pipeline of top-tier scholars to Northwest Florida's largest university. One of the new honorees is a graduate of Tate High School in Santa Rosa County.

The addition brings UWF's total count of National Merit Finalists to 20 students since 2017, according to the university. The competitive designation recognizes exceptional academic achievement and puts these scholars among the nation's top high school performers.

National Merit recognition is considered one of the most prestigious academic honors available to high school seniors. The program identifies students based on PSAT performance and additional academic criteria, making selection to finalist status highly competitive.

UWF has increasingly attracted academically gifted students in recent years, with the National Merit Finalist enrollment representing part of the university's broader efforts to strengthen its academic profile and draw top talent from the region.

item.title: Dolly Parton, Country Music Legend, Dies at 79
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Dolly Parton, the iconic country music star whose career spanned more than six decades, has died. She was 79. Parton was far more than just a musician. The Tennessee native became a cultural institution—a Grammy Award-winning recording artist, actress, philanthropist, and businesswoman whose influence extended well beyond the music industry. Her…
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Parton, the iconic country music star whose career spanned more than six decades, has died. She was 79.

Parton was far more than just a musician. The Tennessee native became a cultural institution—a Grammy Award-winning recording artist, actress, philanthropist, and businesswoman whose influence extended well beyond the music industry. Her songwriting prowess, distinctive voice, and larger-than-life personality made her one of the most recognizable entertainers in American history.

Best known for hits like "Jolene" and "9 to 5," Parton transcended genre boundaries and earned respect across multiple entertainment mediums. She also became known for her charitable work, particularly through the Imagination Library, which has distributed millions of free books to children worldwide.

Parton's legacy extends through generations of artists she influenced and the countless fans who grew up with her music and performances.

The Wind Creek Play of the Week honor recognizes outstanding individual performances from high school football players across the region each week during the season.

item.content:encoded: A Foley, Alabama family made an unexpected discovery when they learned that a man named Richard Daseke had been regularly visiting the grave of their brother, Louis Jones, who died in Vietnam 57 years ago. Mable Rorie, Jones's older sister, occasionally visits her brother's cemetery plot in their hometown, but had no idea about Daseke's quiet tributes until the two connected recently. The chance encounter has given the Jones family new insight into how their fallen loved one's memory has touched the lives of strangers in the community. According to WKRG News 5, the meeting has sparked questions about what drew Daseke to honor Jones's memory and has deepened the family's understanding of their brother's legacy decades after his death in the Vietnam War.

Captain Daniel Arsenault and his crew initially spotted debris in the water—coolers and pool floats—before coming across the unmanned aircraft, according to WKRG…
item.content:encoded:
A routine fishing trip turned into an unexpected salvage operation Saturday when the crew of Hot Spot Fishing Charters discovered a large military drone floating in waters off Pensacola.

Captain Daniel Arsenault and his crew initially spotted debris in the water—coolers and pool floats—before coming across the unmanned aircraft, according to WKRG News 5. The discovery raises questions about how the drone ended up in the Gulf, particularly given the proximity to NAS Pensacola and other military operations in the area.

It's unclear at this point which military branch operated the drone or the circumstances that led to it being in the water. The incident highlights the busy airspace and maritime activity along the Panhandle, where military training and operations are frequent.

The discovery was reported to authorities. NewsRadio Pensacola is working to learn more details about the drone's origin and whether it was recovered.

item.title: Fairhope's Magnolia Beach restoration finished after years of erosion
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: After years of watching waves chip away at its shoreline, Fairhope, Alabama has completed a major restoration project at Magnolia Beach. The work addresses significant erosion that had been steadily reshaping the Eastern Shore landscape, according to the city's engineer Richard Johnson. Visitors to the beach will notice visible changes along the…
item.content:encoded:
After years of watching waves chip away at its shoreline, Fairhope, Alabama has completed a major restoration project at Magnolia Beach. The work addresses significant erosion that had been steadily reshaping the Eastern Shore landscape, according to the city's engineer Richard Johnson.

Visitors to the beach will notice visible changes along the waterfront as the restoration work wraps up. Johnson indicated the project was overdue, given the pace at which the Gulf's waves and tidal action had been eating into the beach.

The completion marks the end of what city officials had identified as a critical need to stabilize and protect one of the area's popular recreational spots. The restored shoreline should provide better protection against future erosion while restoring access and appeal to the beach.

The collision occurred around 3:45 p.m. on the southbound lanes of Highway 29, just south of North Barth Road near Camp O' the Pines. Authorities say the log truck left the roadway and struck a power pole…
item.content:encoded:
A log truck driver was pronounced dead Monday afternoon following a crash on Highway 29 north of Molino, according to North Escambia reports. The collision occurred around 3:45 p.m. on the southbound lanes of Highway 29, just south of North Barth Road near Camp O' the Pines. Authorities say the log truck left the roadway and struck a power pole near the treeline.

The fatal crash remains under investigation. No additional details about the driver's identity or the circumstances leading to the accident have been released at this time.

The incident marks another serious traffic fatality in the North Escambia area. Drivers in the region are urged to exercise caution on Highway 29, particularly in rural stretches where visibility and road conditions can change.
